15	  source: directory-lister
16	quirks:
17	  - "⛔⛔ THIS PUBLISHES EVERYTHING IN THE FOLDER YOU POINT IT AT, TO ANYONE WITH THE URL, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE PRODUCT. Directory Lister browses a directory and serves the files in it. There is no upload, no editing and no write path of any kind, so nothing can be tampered with; there is equally nothing stopping a stranger reading and downloading every file. Before you deploy, the user has to answer one question out loud: is this folder's entire contents fit to be on the public internet? If the answer is anything other than yes, either do not put those files in it or use the password shape described below. Never mount a home directory, a backup directory or anything with credentials in it."
18	  - "⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR, AND WHEN: NOBODY, EVER, BECAUSE THERE ARE NO ACCOUNTS. Upstream states it plainly in docs/configuration/authentication.md:7: Directory Lister does not include any form of authentication out of the box, and that is intentional. There is no signup form, no login page, no admin panel, no API key and no first-user-is-owner rule anywhere in the app; there is exactly ONE route (IndexController.php:20-28) and it serves the listing. So there is no ownership race to lose and no window to close by racing to a form. The corollary is the uncomfortable half: an anonymous visitor has exactly the same rights over this instance as you do, which are read and download. The only way to change that is to put authentication IN FRONT of it, which upstream recommends and which the vhost in the body of this file does."
19	  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH, BY QUERY PARAMETER, BECAUSE IT IS ONE ROUTE AND FIVE BEHAVIOURS. IndexController dispatches on the FIRST query parameter: ?file=<path> streams a file, ?info=<path> returns size, type and md5, sha1 and sha256 hashes, ?search=<term> searches names, ?zip=<dir> streams a zip of a whole directory, and anything else is a directory listing of ?dir=<path>. All five are open to everyone unless something in front of the app says otherwise. There is no rate limiting of any kind."
20	  - "⛔⛔ HIDE_DOT_FILES HIDES FROM THE LISTING AND DOES NOT STOP THE DOWNLOAD. THIS IS THE ONE THAT WILL CATCH SOMEBODY. It defaults to true, so a folder containing a dot file looks clean, and a direct request for that file by name returns 200 with its contents. Measured locally against 5.6.1: the dot file was absent from the listing and ?file= served it in full. The reason is in the code: FinderFactory.php:44-50 applies the dot-file and VCS flags to the FINDER, which only builds the listing, while FileController.php:39 and the file-info controller consult only the hidden-file GLOB. Two different filters, one of which people assume is the other. If a file must not be downloadable, it has to be in the hidden-files list, and the next quirk is how to make that list work at all."
21	  - "⛔ THE .hidden FILE IN YOUR DATA DIRECTORY DOES NOTHING UNLESS YOU SET HIDDEN_FILES_LIST. app/config/app.php:110 defaults hidden_files_list to the RELATIVE path .hidden, which is resolved with is_readable() against the process working directory. Under Apache in this image that is the application root, not your data directory, so the file every tutorial tells you to create is silently never read. Measured: with a .hidden in the data directory and nothing else, the named file was still listed and still downloadable; with HIDDEN_FILES_LIST=/data/.hidden set, the same file returned 404 from both ?file= and ?info= and vanished from the listing. Set the variable to an absolute path, always. ⚠️ Note also that the compiled container is cached on first run, so edits to the hidden list want a container restart, and treat the list as a tidiness feature rather than a security boundary: the safe design is to not put the file in the published folder."
22	  - "⛔ TRAVERSAL OUT OF THE DATA DIRECTORY WORKS, UP TO A LIMIT THAT IS SET IN CODE RATHER THAN CONFIG, AND THE CONSEQUENCE IS A REAL RULE. app/config/container.php:115 builds the path by concatenating files_path with whatever arrives in the query string, and nothing in the app constrains the result. The only guard is index.php:15, which sets open_basedir at runtime to the application directory plus FILES_PATH. Measured against 5.6.1: ?file=../etc/passwd was refused, with a PHP warning that helpfully printed the allowed paths, while ?dir=../var/www/html listed the application directory and ?file=../var/www/html/.env.example returned its contents. THE RULE THAT FOLLOWS: configure this app with ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES and never with a .env file in the application root, because such a file is world readable by direct URL. Upstream's app_files list does hide .env, but IsHidden.php:23-25 anchors that pattern at FILES_PATH, so it protects a .env in your DATA folder and not the one the docs tell you to create."
23	  - "⛔ ZIP_DOWNLOADS DEFAULTS TO TRUE AND IS AN ANONYMOUS AMPLIFIER. app/config/app.php:79. Any visitor can ask the server to walk a directory and stream it as a zip; measured, ?zip=../var/www/html produced an 18 MB archive of the application directory from one unauthenticated request. Combine that with php.prod.ini setting memory_limit = -1 and with ?info= hashing files up to MAX_HASH_SIZE, which defaults to a full gigabyte and computes three digests over it, and you have three cheap ways for a stranger to spend your CPU and your egress. For a public instance set ZIP_DOWNLOADS=false unless the user specifically wants folder downloads, and lower MAX_HASH_SIZE. The zip does respect the hidden-file list, because ZipController uses the same Finder as the listing."
24	  - "⛔ THE TRIAL EGRESS ALLOWANCE IS 5 GB AND THIS IS THE ONE APP IN THE LIBRARY WHOSE ENTIRE JOB IS EGRESS. From redu's own billing code: a carded account gets 2 TB of free egress a month, a no-card trial account gets 5 GB by default. A file browser on a public hostname is exactly the workload that turns that into a bill, and it can be spent by strangers rather than by the user. Say the number BEFORE deploying, not after. If the plan is to publish anything sizeable to the public, this wants a card and probably ZIP_DOWNLOADS=false."
25	  - "PUTTING A PASSWORD IN FRONT OF IT: VERIFIED, AND IT IS THE ONLY MITIGATION UPSTREAM ENDORSES. The image is php:8.5-apache, so Apache's own basic auth is available with no extra software. Mount a vhost file over /etc/apache2/sites-available/000-default.conf that adds AuthType Basic over the document root, plus an AuthUserFile you generate with the htpasswd binary already inside the image. Measured on 5.6.1: anonymous requests to /, ?file= and ?zip= all returned 401, a correct credential returned 200 and served the file, and a wrong one returned 401. The exact files are in the body of this document. Note this is ONE shared credential for everyone, not per-person accounts, and Apache basic auth sends it on every request, which is fine here only because redu terminates TLS in front of the container."
26	  - "PORT: THE CONTAINER LISTENS ON 80 AND THIS RECIPE PUBLISHES IT ON HOST PORT 8080. The Dockerfile exposes 80 and Apache's vhost listens there; nothing supports changing the internal port, so map it rather than fight it. Pass 8080 to deploy_compose. Health probe: GET / , which returns 200 with the string Directory Lister in the body on a healthy instance. ⚠️ If you add the basic-auth vhost, / answers 401 to an unauthenticated probe, so point any uptime monitor at it WITH the credential or it will report a permanent outage."
27	  - "⛔ DELETE THE SERVICES IN THE REPO'S OWN docker-compose.yaml. That file builds the DEV target from source and brings up redis, memcached and an npm watcher; it is a development harness and not a deployment. The compose to copy is the small one in upstream's docker.md, which is what the body of this file contains. Caching needs nothing extra: app/config/cache.php:20,45 default the app cache to file and the view cache to a directory inside the container, so a managed Redis here would be paid for and never used."
28	  - "GETTING FILES IN, AND WHERE THEY LIVE, WHICH IS THE PRACTICAL QUESTION THIS APP RAISES AND NOTHING ELSE IN THE LIBRARY DOES. There is no upload feature, by design. Two honest routes. (1) Ship the files WITH the deploy: put them in a files/ directory beside the compose and bind-mount ./files:/data:ro. Read-only is correct, since the app never writes to the data directory, and it means the set is reproduced exactly on every redeploy. (2) Copy them onto the VM afterwards over ssh into a named Docker volume mounted at /data. ⚠️ Either way the files live on the APP VM's disk. There is no managed database and no separate storage service holding them, so deleting the deployment deletes the library. Say that plainly, and if the content matters, back it up somewhere off the VM."
29	  - "⛔ DISK IS THE REAL CONSTRAINT, NOT MEMORY, AND IT IS A DECISION TO PUT TO THE USER BEFORE SIZING. The flavor's disk is what you get: m1.small brings 20 GB, m1.medium 40 GB and m1.large 80 GB, and the Ubuntu install plus this 726 MB image come out of it before a single file of the user's does. Growing it later is a volume resize rather than a redeploy, so ask up front how large the library is and how fast it grows. Memory is not the issue: the app is a PHP process per request with no database, and the local container idled around 31 MiB, which is a laptop reading and not a redu one."
30	  - "SET APP_DEBUG=false AND LEAVE IT THERE. It is the default in .env.example, and it is what keeps the Whoops error handler from rendering stack traces, file paths and configuration to an anonymous visitor on any unexpected error. On an app with no authentication that page is the largest single information leak available, so never turn it on to debug a live instance."

The registry ALSO carries a master tag, updated 2026-08-11 and therefore the newest by date, which is the development branch: any tooling that sorts tags by date and takes the top one installs it. Pin the exact version, and never write :latest into a recipe."
32	  - "SIZING AND COST: m1.small, no managed database, roughly GBP 0.0174/hr and GBP 13 a month, which fits the no-card free trial on flavor. Read the egress quirk before treating the trial as free for this particular app. Do NOT pass db_flavor_id or db_engine; there is nothing to connect to."

repo: https://github.com/DirectoryLister/DirectoryLister
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: directorylister/directorylister:5.6.1
  port: 8080
  vm: m1.small
  flavor_id: "2"

  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: directory-lister
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ THIS PUBLISHES EVERYTHING IN THE FOLDER YOU POINT IT AT, TO ANYONE WITH THE URL, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE PRODUCT. Directory Lister browses a directory and serves the files in it. There is no upload, no editing and no write path of any kind, so nothing can be tampered with; there is equally nothing stopping a stranger reading and downloading every file. Before you deploy, the user has to answer one question out loud: is this folder's entire contents fit to be on the public internet? If the answer is anything other than yes, either do not put those files in it or use the password shape described below. Never mount a home directory, a backup directory or anything with credentials in it."
  - "⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR, AND WHEN: NOBODY, EVER, BECAUSE THERE ARE NO ACCOUNTS. Upstream states it plainly in docs/configuration/authentication.md:7: Directory Lister does not include any form of authentication out of the box, and that is intentional. There is no signup form, no login page, no admin panel, no API key and no first-user-is-owner rule anywhere in the app; there is exactly ONE route (IndexController.php:20-28) and it serves the listing. So there is no ownership race to lose and no window to close by racing to a form. The corollary is the uncomfortable half: an anonymous visitor has exactly the same rights over this instance as you do, which are read and download. The only way to change that is to put authentication IN FRONT of it, which upstream recommends and which the vhost in the body of this file does."
  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH, BY QUERY PARAMETER, BECAUSE IT IS ONE ROUTE AND FIVE BEHAVIOURS. IndexController dispatches on the FIRST query parameter: ?file=<path> streams a file, ?info=<path> returns size, type and md5, sha1 and sha256 hashes, ?search=<term> searches names, ?zip=<dir> streams a zip of a whole directory, and anything else is a directory listing of ?dir=<path>. All five are open to everyone unless something in front of the app says otherwise. There is no rate limiting of any kind."
  - "⛔⛔ HIDE_DOT_FILES HIDES FROM THE LISTING AND DOES NOT STOP THE DOWNLOAD. THIS IS THE ONE THAT WILL CATCH SOMEBODY. It defaults to true, so a folder containing a dot file looks clean, and a direct request for that file by name returns 200 with its contents. Measured locally against 5.6.1: the dot file was absent from the listing and ?file= served it in full. The reason is in the code: FinderFactory.php:44-50 applies the dot-file and VCS flags to the FINDER, which only builds the listing, while FileController.php:39 and the file-info controller consult only the hidden-file GLOB. Two different filters, one of which people assume is the other. If a file must not be downloadable, it has to be in the hidden-files list, and the next quirk is how to make that list work at all."
  - "⛔ THE .hidden FILE IN YOUR DATA DIRECTORY DOES NOTHING UNLESS YOU SET HIDDEN_FILES_LIST. app/config/app.php:110 defaults hidden_files_list to the RELATIVE path .hidden, which is resolved with is_readable() against the process working directory. Under Apache in this image that is the application root, not your data directory, so the file every tutorial tells you to create is silently never read. Measured: with a .hidden in the data directory and nothing else, the named file was still listed and still downloadable; with HIDDEN_FILES_LIST=/data/.hidden set, the same file returned 404 from both ?file= and ?info= and vanished from the listing. Set the variable to an absolute path, always. ⚠️ Note also that the compiled container is cached on first run, so edits to the hidden list want a container restart, and treat the list as a tidiness feature rather than a security boundary: the safe design is to not put the file in the published folder."
  - "⛔ TRAVERSAL OUT OF THE DATA DIRECTORY WORKS, UP TO A LIMIT THAT IS SET IN CODE RATHER THAN CONFIG, AND THE CONSEQUENCE IS A REAL RULE. app/config/container.php:115 builds the path by concatenating files_path with whatever arrives in the query string, and nothing in the app constrains the result. The only guard is index.php:15, which sets open_basedir at runtime to the application directory plus FILES_PATH. Measured against 5.6.1: ?file=../etc/passwd was refused, with a PHP warning that helpfully printed the allowed paths, while ?dir=../var/www/html listed the application directory and ?file=../var/www/html/.env.example returned its contents. THE RULE THAT FOLLOWS: configure this app with ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES and never with a .env file in the application root, because such a file is world readable by direct URL. Upstream's app_files list does hide .env, but IsHidden.php:23-25 anchors that pattern at FILES_PATH, so it protects a .env in your DATA folder and not the one the docs tell you to create."
  - "⛔ ZIP_DOWNLOADS DEFAULTS TO TRUE AND IS AN ANONYMOUS AMPLIFIER. app/config/app.php:79. Any visitor can ask the server to walk a directory and stream it as a zip; measured, ?zip=../var/www/html produced an 18 MB archive of the application directory from one unauthenticated request. Combine that with php.prod.ini setting memory_limit = -1 and with ?info= hashing files up to MAX_HASH_SIZE, which defaults to a full gigabyte and computes three digests over it, and you have three cheap ways for a stranger to spend your CPU and your egress. For a public instance set ZIP_DOWNLOADS=false unless the user specifically wants folder downloads, and lower MAX_HASH_SIZE. The zip does respect the hidden-file list, because ZipController uses the same Finder as the listing."
  - "⛔ THE TRIAL EGRESS ALLOWANCE IS 5 GB AND THIS IS THE ONE APP IN THE LIBRARY WHOSE ENTIRE JOB IS EGRESS. From redu's own billing code: a carded account gets 2 TB of free egress a month, a no-card trial account gets 5 GB by default. A file browser on a public hostname is exactly the workload that turns that into a bill, and it can be spent by strangers rather than by the user. Say the number BEFORE deploying, not after. If the plan is to publish anything sizeable to the public, this wants a card and probably ZIP_DOWNLOADS=false."
  - "PUTTING A PASSWORD IN FRONT OF IT: VERIFIED, AND IT IS THE ONLY MITIGATION UPSTREAM ENDORSES. The image is php:8.5-apache, so Apache's own basic auth is available with no extra software. Mount a vhost file over /etc/apache2/sites-available/000-default.conf that adds AuthType Basic over the document root, plus an AuthUserFile you generate with the htpasswd binary already inside the image. Measured on 5.6.1: anonymous requests to /, ?file= and ?zip= all returned 401, a correct credential returned 200 and served the file, and a wrong one returned 401. The exact files are in the body of this document. Note this is ONE shared credential for everyone, not per-person accounts, and Apache basic auth sends it on every request, which is fine here only because redu terminates TLS in front of the container."
  - "PORT: THE CONTAINER LISTENS ON 80 AND THIS RECIPE PUBLISHES IT ON HOST PORT 8080. The Dockerfile exposes 80 and Apache's vhost listens there; nothing supports changing the internal port, so map it rather than fight it. Pass 8080 to deploy_compose. Health probe: GET / , which returns 200 with the string Directory Lister in the body on a healthy instance. ⚠️ If you add the basic-auth vhost, / answers 401 to an unauthenticated probe, so point any uptime monitor at it WITH the credential or it will report a permanent outage."
  - "⛔ DELETE THE SERVICES IN THE REPO'S OWN docker-compose.yaml. That file builds the DEV target from source and brings up redis, memcached and an npm watcher; it is a development harness and not a deployment. The compose to copy is the small one in upstream's docker.md, which is what the body of this file contains. Caching needs nothing extra: app/config/cache.php:20,45 default the app cache to file and the view cache to a directory inside the container, so a managed Redis here would be paid for and never used."
  - "GETTING FILES IN, AND WHERE THEY LIVE, WHICH IS THE PRACTICAL QUESTION THIS APP RAISES AND NOTHING ELSE IN THE LIBRARY DOES. There is no upload feature, by design. Two honest routes. (1) Ship the files WITH the deploy: put them in a files/ directory beside the compose and bind-mount ./files:/data:ro. Read-only is correct, since the app never writes to the data directory, and it means the set is reproduced exactly on every redeploy. (2) Copy them onto the VM afterwards over ssh into a named Docker volume mounted at /data. ⚠️ Either way the files live on the APP VM's disk. There is no managed database and no separate storage service holding them, so deleting the deployment deletes the library. Say that plainly, and if the content matters, back it up somewhere off the VM."
  - "⛔ DISK IS THE REAL CONSTRAINT, NOT MEMORY, AND IT IS A DECISION TO PUT TO THE USER BEFORE SIZING. The flavor's disk is what you get: m1.small brings 20 GB, m1.medium 40 GB and m1.large 80 GB, and the Ubuntu install plus this 726 MB image come out of it before a single file of the user's does. Growing it later is a volume resize rather than a redeploy, so ask up front how large the library is and how fast it grows. Memory is not the issue: the app is a PHP process per request with no database, and the local container idled around 31 MiB, which is a laptop reading and not a redu one."
  - "SET APP_DEBUG=false AND LEAVE IT THERE. It is the default in .env.example, and it is what keeps the Whoops error handler from rendering stack traces, file paths and configuration to an anonymous visitor on any unexpected error. On an app with no authentication that page is the largest single information leak available, so never turn it on to debug a live instance."
  - "PIN THE IMAGE AND MIND THE master TAG. directorylister/directorylister:5.6.1 was published 2026-07-02 and carries the same digest as latest, 5 and 5.6. The registry ALSO carries a master tag, updated 2026-08-11 and therefore the newest by date, which is the development branch: any tooling that sorts tags by date and takes the top one installs it. Pin the exact version, and never write :latest into a recipe."
  - "SIZING AND COST: m1.small, no managed database, roughly GBP 0.0174/hr and GBP 13 a month, which fits the no-card free trial on flavor. Read the egress quirk before treating the trial as free for this particular app. Do NOT pass db_flavor_id or db_engine; there is nothing to connect to."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> establish WITH THE USER what folder is being published and that its whole contents may be public -> decide whether it is open or behind the basic-auth vhost, and if behind it, generate the credential -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan, the cost and the 5 GB trial egress allowance and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '2' (m1.small), no database, port 8080. plan_deploy will want to upsize a compose stack to m1.large, which is the right default for things that BUILD from source and wrong here, since the image is pulled; passing flavor_id '2' explicitly holds m1.small."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built. Write the compose locally, add the vhost and credential file if you are closing it, add a files/ directory if you are shipping content with the deploy, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."
  - "LICENCE: MIT, from the LICENSE file in the repository root, copyright Chris Kankiewicz. Permissive, no network clause, no additional conditions and nothing for a self-hoster to reason about beyond keeping the notice. The default page footer credits Directory Lister; leaving it there is the polite thing to do and costs nothing."
  - "DELETING IT DELETES THE PUBLISHED FILES. There is no managed database to leave behind, so nothing keeps billing afterwards, and equally nothing survives: the volume goes with the app VM. Say both halves before deleting."

---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/DirectoryLister/DirectoryLister
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: directorylister/directorylister:5.6.1
  port: 8080
  vm: m1.small
  flavor_id: "2"
  database: "none. Directory Lister has no database; it reads a folder"
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0174
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: directory-lister
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ THIS PUBLISHES EVERYTHING IN THE FOLDER YOU POINT IT AT, TO ANYONE WITH THE URL, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE PRODUCT. Directory Lister browses a directory and serves the files in it. There is no upload, no editing and no write path of any kind, so nothing can be tampered with; there is equally nothing stopping a stranger reading and downloading every file. Before you deploy, the user has to answer one question out loud: is this folder's entire contents fit to be on the public internet? If the answer is anything other than yes, either do not put those files in it or use the password shape described below. Never mount a home directory, a backup directory or anything with credentials in it."
  - "⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR, AND WHEN: NOBODY, EVER, BECAUSE THERE ARE NO ACCOUNTS. Upstream states it plainly in docs/configuration/authentication.md:7: Directory Lister does not include any form of authentication out of the box, and that is intentional. There is no signup form, no login page, no admin panel, no API key and no first-user-is-owner rule anywhere in the app; there is exactly ONE route (IndexController.php:20-28) and it serves the listing. So there is no ownership race to lose and no window to close by racing to a form. The corollary is the uncomfortable half: an anonymous visitor has exactly the same rights over this instance as you do, which are read and download. The only way to change that is to put authentication IN FRONT of it, which upstream recommends and which the vhost in the body of this file does."
  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH, BY QUERY PARAMETER, BECAUSE IT IS ONE ROUTE AND FIVE BEHAVIOURS. IndexController dispatches on the FIRST query parameter: ?file=<path> streams a file, ?info=<path> returns size, type and md5, sha1 and sha256 hashes, ?search=<term> searches names, ?zip=<dir> streams a zip of a whole directory, and anything else is a directory listing of ?dir=<path>. All five are open to everyone unless something in front of the app says otherwise. There is no rate limiting of any kind."
  - "⛔⛔ HIDE_DOT_FILES HIDES FROM THE LISTING AND DOES NOT STOP THE DOWNLOAD. THIS IS THE ONE THAT WILL CATCH SOMEBODY. It defaults to true, so a folder containing a dot file looks clean, and a direct request for that file by name returns 200 with its contents. Measured locally against 5.6.1: the dot file was absent from the listing and ?file= served it in full. The reason is in the code: FinderFactory.php:44-50 applies the dot-file and VCS flags to the FINDER, which only builds the listing, while FileController.php:39 and the file-info controller consult only the hidden-file GLOB. Two different filters, one of which people assume is the other. If a file must not be downloadable, it has to be in the hidden-files list, and the next quirk is how to make that list work at all."
  - "⛔ THE .hidden FILE IN YOUR DATA DIRECTORY DOES NOTHING UNLESS YOU SET HIDDEN_FILES_LIST. app/config/app.php:110 defaults hidden_files_list to the RELATIVE path .hidden, which is resolved with is_readable() against the process working directory. Under Apache in this image that is the application root, not your data directory, so the file every tutorial tells you to create is silently never read. Measured: with a .hidden in the data directory and nothing else, the named file was still listed and still downloadable; with HIDDEN_FILES_LIST=/data/.hidden set, the same file returned 404 from both ?file= and ?info= and vanished from the listing. Set the variable to an absolute path, always. ⚠️ Note also that the compiled container is cached on first run, so edits to the hidden list want a container restart, and treat the list as a tidiness feature rather than a security boundary: the safe design is to not put the file in the published folder."
  - "⛔ TRAVERSAL OUT OF THE DATA DIRECTORY WORKS, UP TO A LIMIT THAT IS SET IN CODE RATHER THAN CONFIG, AND THE CONSEQUENCE IS A REAL RULE. app/config/container.php:115 builds the path by concatenating files_path with whatever arrives in the query string, and nothing in the app constrains the result. The only guard is index.php:15, which sets open_basedir at runtime to the application directory plus FILES_PATH. Measured against 5.6.1: ?file=../etc/passwd was refused, with a PHP warning that helpfully printed the allowed paths, while ?dir=../var/www/html listed the application directory and ?file=../var/www/html/.env.example returned its contents. THE RULE THAT FOLLOWS: configure this app with ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES and never with a .env file in the application root, because such a file is world readable by direct URL. Upstream's app_files list does hide .env, but IsHidden.php:23-25 anchors that pattern at FILES_PATH, so it protects a .env in your DATA folder and not the one the docs tell you to create."
  - "⛔ ZIP_DOWNLOADS DEFAULTS TO TRUE AND IS AN ANONYMOUS AMPLIFIER. app/config/app.php:79. Any visitor can ask the server to walk a directory and stream it as a zip; measured, ?zip=../var/www/html produced an 18 MB archive of the application directory from one unauthenticated request. Combine that with php.prod.ini setting memory_limit = -1 and with ?info= hashing files up to MAX_HASH_SIZE, which defaults to a full gigabyte and computes three digests over it, and you have three cheap ways for a stranger to spend your CPU and your egress. For a public instance set ZIP_DOWNLOADS=false unless the user specifically wants folder downloads, and lower MAX_HASH_SIZE. The zip does respect the hidden-file list, because ZipController uses the same Finder as the listing."
  - "⛔ THE TRIAL EGRESS ALLOWANCE IS 5 GB AND THIS IS THE ONE APP IN THE LIBRARY WHOSE ENTIRE JOB IS EGRESS. From redu's own billing code: a carded account gets 2 TB of free egress a month, a no-card trial account gets 5 GB by default. A file browser on a public hostname is exactly the workload that turns that into a bill, and it can be spent by strangers rather than by the user. Say the number BEFORE deploying, not after. If the plan is to publish anything sizeable to the public, this wants a card and probably ZIP_DOWNLOADS=false."
  - "PUTTING A PASSWORD IN FRONT OF IT: VERIFIED, AND IT IS THE ONLY MITIGATION UPSTREAM ENDORSES. The image is php:8.5-apache, so Apache's own basic auth is available with no extra software. Mount a vhost file over /etc/apache2/sites-available/000-default.conf that adds AuthType Basic over the document root, plus an AuthUserFile you generate with the htpasswd binary already inside the image. Measured on 5.6.1: anonymous requests to /, ?file= and ?zip= all returned 401, a correct credential returned 200 and served the file, and a wrong one returned 401. The exact files are in the body of this document. Note this is ONE shared credential for everyone, not per-person accounts, and Apache basic auth sends it on every request, which is fine here only because redu terminates TLS in front of the container."
  - "PORT: THE CONTAINER LISTENS ON 80 AND THIS RECIPE PUBLISHES IT ON HOST PORT 8080. The Dockerfile exposes 80 and Apache's vhost listens there; nothing supports changing the internal port, so map it rather than fight it. Pass 8080 to deploy_compose. Health probe: GET / , which returns 200 with the string Directory Lister in the body on a healthy instance. ⚠️ If you add the basic-auth vhost, / answers 401 to an unauthenticated probe, so point any uptime monitor at it WITH the credential or it will report a permanent outage."
  - "⛔ DELETE THE SERVICES IN THE REPO'S OWN docker-compose.yaml. That file builds the DEV target from source and brings up redis, memcached and an npm watcher; it is a development harness and not a deployment. The compose to copy is the small one in upstream's docker.md, which is what the body of this file contains.
